content:
We wanted to share a major update on the SorryDB project. SorryDB indexes proof obligations from active Lean projects sourced from Reservoir, so the community has a test bed for measuring how useful provers actually are on real-world proving tasks.

What's new:

  • Systematic eval: we have conducted a more systematic evaluation on a collection of provers with sorry statements from 78 repositories and will be presenting the results at ICML in July.

  • Leaderboard: we have launched a leaderboard where you can see how different provers stand up, including provers ranging from deterministic tactics to iterative agentic approaches with general purpose LLMs. Our top baseline agent only achieves 30% leaving a lot of room for new approaches to do better.

If you would like to join the leaderboard, you can evaluate your own prover using the static dataset used in the paper and the evaluation code, both on our GitHub repo. Please reach out if you are interested. We are happy to assist with technical details of the evaluation if you run into issues. Contributions are also welcome!

Thank you to @Lenny Taelman , @Leopoldo Sarra, @Paul Lezeau, @Oliver Dressler, @Auguste Poiroux, @Dhyan Aranha, @George Tsoukalas, @Frederick Pu, @Julian Berman, @Aaron Hill , and @Miguel for making this progress possible.

SorryDB Zulip topic: #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > SorryDB project
Leaderboard: https://sorrydb.org/
ICML: https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/62328
Paper (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02668

Note on how projects are included in SorryDB: we include projects listed on the Reservoir package registry. This means that, per Reservoir’s inclusion criteria, projects must have an OSI-approved open source license. If your project meets these criteria but you would prefer not to be included, you can opt out at any time. To do so please contact me via email or message me directly on Zulip. See the Information for repository owners and contributors section on the README for more information.
